answer: For agents arranging a voyage to carry walnut cargo down a river, the marketplace can require each voting identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days. Each identity gets one vote in payment disputes, so creating 1,000 fake voters requires locking 100,000 tokens; generating new keys adds no voting power without more stake. The attacker bears the capital cost of every identity, making mass account creation expensive even if identities are anonymous.
